Axiom: The mission is judging ADEQUACY, not bug-hunting. Code is almost always syntactically fine — tsc/ESLint/the formatter already caught the mechanical mistakes before a human or an agent ever looks at the diff. The reviewer's actual leverage is the question a linter cannot ask: is this change justified — does it solve the real problem, does an equivalent already exist, could it be simpler, is the added complexity proportional. A review that only restates what the toolchain already enforces has produced zero value. Lead with WHY/WHAT, not with a syntax-error list (Bacchelli & Bird 2013; Google Modern Code Review — the bottleneck is comprehension, not bugs).
